placements.why: The envelope's entire content is an instrument-calibration record — a named spectrograph brought to a specific frequency and checked against dated reference plates across its operating band. Nothing in the supplied (empty) strata covers organizational work of this kind, and calibration/verification is a recognizable organizational-strategy category distinct from Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates already named in the taxonomy's pattern — it names a subject future calibration envelopes will keep feeding, not a one-time fact.
placements.title: Calibration work as its own organizational category
placements.frame: Does this content describe calibrating or verifying an instrument's operational readiness against a reference standard?

placements.title: Instrument readiness established through reference-verified calibration
placements.frame: What instrument was calibrated, against what reference standard, and does the verification hold across its full intended operating range?
placements.why: All three segments converge on one theme: the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration state, established and confirmed by verification against dated reference plates, holding across the observing band. src-1 states it in narrative prose; src-2 and src-3 restate the same claim as structured fielded-spec entries (instrument identity, calibration value). This is a subject future calibration envelopes for this or other instruments would keep feeding — not a one-time measurement, which the grain test flags as fact-not-leaf. No existing leaf was supplied to reuse, so this is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
